-- Bronze: Kinetic company enrollment gate, reused directly, not rebuilt (SD-10).
-- Never hardcode a Kinetic company list anywhere downstream -- join to this model.

select
    company       as company_code,
    isactive      as is_active_raw,
    fiscalyear_start,
    fiscalperiod_start,
    fiscalyear_end,
    fiscalperiod_end
from MATILLION_RAW.CRETEX_EPICOR_KINETIC.CTXEPICORKINETIC_V_ANALYTICS_COMPANY_ENROLLMENT
where isactive = 'Y'

-- Gold: conformed part dimension, reused read-only from the DW (SD-18) -- not rebuilt.
-- Matches production's own REF_PART_DIM sourcing decision. Filtered to our 3 Kinetic
-- companies only (ProfitKey's '14'/'32' excluded -- out of scope per SD-01).
-- Key = part_dim_key, already provided by the DW (company + part + revision, resolved).

select
    companyid_part_rev_source_parthk_key   as part_dim_key,
    company_id,
    part_number                            as part_key,
    revision_number                        as part_revision,
    part_source,
    internal_part_number,
    external_part_number,
    part_desc,
    part_desc_2,
    revshortdesc                           as rev_short_desc,
    revdescription                         as rev_description,
    prod_code                              as product_code,
    type_code,
    part_class_desc,
    commercial_category,
    commercial_sub_category,
    approved,
    approved_date,
    effective_date,
    part_uses_inventory,
    part_deleted_date,
    part_deleted_flag,
    part_rev_deleted_date,
    part_rev_deleted_flag,
    part_intro_date,
    part_age_years,
    part_age_months
from PRD_DW.DATAMART.T_DIMPART_ALLERPS
where company_id in ('CTX11002', 'CTX11003', 'CTX11101')

-- Gold: fiscal calendar, reused read-only from the DW (SD-18) -- not rebuilt.
-- Matches production's own REF_DATE sourcing decision. Key = date_key itself:
-- a date dimension's natural key is already stable and unique, so no hash surrogate
-- is needed here (a deliberate, documented exception to hashing every key).
-- Target lag matches the pipeline's 1-hour cadence (not daily, despite rarely changing)
-- to stay compatible with downstream Dynamic Tables that join it (a Dynamic Table's lag
-- can't be tighter than its upstream's).

select
    onlydate                as calendar_date,
    dateyyyymmdd             as date_key,

    calendaryear             as calendar_year,
    calendarmonth            as calendar_month,
    calendarmonthname        as calendar_month_name,
    calendardayofweekname    as day_of_week_name,

    fiscalyear               as fiscal_year,
    fiscalmonth              as fiscal_month,
    fiscalperiod             as fiscal_period,
    fiscalmonthdisplay       as fiscal_month_display,
    fiscalmonthdisplaysort   as fiscal_month_display_sort,
    fiscalweek               as fiscal_week,
    fiscalweekdisplay        as fiscal_week_display,
    fiscalquarteryear        as fiscal_quarter_year,
    fiscalquarterdisplay     as fiscal_quarter_display,
    fiscalstartofmonth       as fiscal_start_of_month,
    fiscalendofmonth         as fiscal_end_of_month,
    fiscalstartofyear        as fiscal_start_of_year,
    fiscalendofyear          as fiscal_end_of_year,
    isfiscalmonthend         as is_fiscal_month_end

from PRD_DW.DATAMART.V_CRETEX_CALENDAR_DATE_DIM

-- Bronze: Kinetic job-costing department master. Thin rename only.
-- Gated by the enrollment view (SD-10).
--
-- SD-22: jc_dept is normalized with upper(trim()) defensively, for join consistency
-- with the other models' jc_dept -- confirmed 0 case variance in this table itself.

with source as (

    select
        company                 as company_code,
        upper(trim(jcdept))     as jc_dept,
        description             as department_description,
        globaljcdept            as is_global_jc_dept,
        sysrevid                as _sysrevid
    from MATILLION_RAW.CRETEX_EPICOR_KINETIC.ERP_JCDEPT

)

select source.*, current_timestamp() as _loaded_at
from source
inner join SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.BRONZE.stg_ctxepicorkinetic__company_enrollment as gate
    on source.company_code = gate.company_code

-- Bronze: Kinetic employee master. Thin rename only. Gated by the enrollment view (SD-10).
-- jc_dept (JCDEPT) is the job-costing department -- the reporting one. The separate
-- DEPARTMENT column is free-text HR data and is deliberately not carried as the
-- reporting department (same column trap production documents).
--
-- SD-22: emp_id is normalized with upper(trim()) -- see
-- stg_ctxepicorkinetic__labor_detail for the empirical case-variance finding.

with source as (

    select
        company                 as company_code,
        upper(trim(empid))      as emp_id,
        name                    as full_name,
        firstname               as first_name,
        lastname                as last_name,
        upper(trim(jcdept))     as jc_dept,
        shift                   as shift_num,
        laborrate               as labor_rate,
        empstatus               as employee_status,
        productionworker        as is_production_worker,
        enrollmentdate          as enrollment_date_text,
        departuredate           as departure_date_text,
        sysrevid                as _sysrevid
    from MATILLION_RAW.CRETEX_EPICOR_KINETIC.ERP_EMPBASIC

)

select source.*, current_timestamp() as _loaded_at
from source
inner join SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.BRONZE.stg_ctxepicorkinetic__company_enrollment as gate
    on source.company_code = gate.company_code

-- Bronze: Kinetic job header. Thin rename only. Gated by the enrollment view (SD-10).
-- planned_start_quantity_not_produced -- renamed from PRODQTY (production's own trap:
-- this is the PLANNED quantity, not what was actually produced; do not mistake it for
-- quantity_produced on labor_detail/job_operation).
--
-- SD-22: job_num, part_num, part_revision are normalized with upper(trim()) -- see
-- stg_ctxepicorkinetic__labor_detail for the empirical case-variance finding. part_num /
-- part_revision case variance is also a contributing cause of the part-match-rate gap
-- (SD-21).

with source as (

    select
        company                             as company_code,
        upper(trim(jobnum))                 as job_num,
        upper(trim(partnum))                as part_num,
        upper(trim(revisionnum))            as part_revision,
        partdescription                     as part_description,
        prodqty                             as planned_start_quantity_not_produced,
        jobtype                             as job_type,
        jobengineered                       as is_job_engineered,
        jobcomplete                         as is_job_complete,
        jobclosed                           as is_job_closed,
        startdate                           as start_date_text,
        duedate                             as due_date_text,
        plant                               as plant,
        (upper(trim(jobnum)) like 'MRP-%')  as is_mrp_planning_job,
        sysrevid                            as _sysrevid
    from MATILLION_RAW.CRETEX_EPICOR_KINETIC.ERP_JOBHEAD

)

-- is_mrp_planning_job: MRP-suggested planning jobs carry large estimated hours against
-- zero produced quantity. They do not affect earned hours (which is driven by quantity
-- produced), but would badly pollute any budget/estimate-side rollup if not flagged --
-- a real source-data fact, not a stylistic choice (confirmed against the production
-- build's own documented investigation of this pattern).

select source.*, current_timestamp() as _loaded_at
from source
inner join SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.BRONZE.stg_ctxepicorkinetic__company_enrollment as gate
    on source.company_code = gate.company_code

-- Gold: conformed department dimension, from Bronze. Built for completeness/future
-- grains -- NOT joined into fct_labor below, since production's own
-- EARNED_HOURS_JOB_OPERATION grain doesn't carry department either (verified via its
-- column list: job/operation/part/resource, no department).

select
    md5(concat_ws('|',coalesce(cast(company_code as varchar), '_surrogate_key_null_'),coalesce(cast(jc_dept as varchar), '_surrogate_key_null_'))) as department_key,
    company_code,
    jc_dept,
    department_description,
    is_global_jc_dept
from SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.BRONZE.stg_ctxepicorkinetic__department

-- Gold: conformed employee dimension, from Bronze.

select
    md5(concat_ws('|',coalesce(cast(company_code as varchar), '_surrogate_key_null_'),coalesce(cast(emp_id as varchar), '_surrogate_key_null_'))) as employee_key,
    company_code,
    emp_id,
    full_name,
    first_name,
    last_name,
    jc_dept,
    shift_num,
    labor_rate,
    employee_status,
    is_production_worker,
    enrollment_date_text,
    departure_date_text
from SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.BRONZE.stg_ctxepicorkinetic__employee

-- Bronze: Kinetic job operations -- the only place Kinetic standard hours live.
-- Thin rename only. Gated by the enrollment view (SD-10). Carries BOTH candidate
-- standards (est_production_hours = budget, NOT earned hours; production_standard_raw +
-- standard_format = the per-unit rate Silver must convert and multiply by quantity
-- produced -- SD-11). No conversion happens here; that is Silver's job.
--
-- SD-22: job_num and operation_code are normalized with upper(trim()) -- see
-- stg_ctxepicorkinetic__labor_detail for the empirical case-variance finding.
--
-- SD-26: setup_pct_complete added -- carries ERP_JOBOPER.SETUPPCTCOMPLETE, needed for the
-- corrected Setup earned-hours formula (read from production's own documented business
-- rules, not re-derived). See int_labor_standard_hours for the formula itself.

with source as (

    select
        company                 as company_code,
        upper(trim(jobnum))     as job_num,
        assemblyseq             as assembly_seqnum,
        oprseq                  as operation_seqnum,
        upper(trim(opcode))     as operation_code,
        subcontract             as is_subcontract,
        runqty                  as run_quantity,
        estsethours             as est_setup_hours,
        estprodhours            as est_production_hours,
        prodstandard            as production_standard_raw,
        stdformat               as standard_format,
        stdbasis                as standard_basis,
        opsperpart              as ops_per_part,
        qtyper                  as quantity_per,
        qtypercycle             as quantity_per_cycle,
        actprodhours            as act_production_hours,
        actsetuphours           as act_setup_hours,
        qtycompleted            as quantity_completed,
        setuppctcomplete        as setup_pct_complete,
        jobengineered           as is_job_engineered,
        opcomplete              as is_operation_complete,
        jobcomplete             as is_job_complete,
        sysrevid                as _sysrevid
    from MATILLION_RAW.CRETEX_EPICOR_KINETIC.ERP_JOBOPER

)

select source.*, current_timestamp() as _loaded_at
from source
inner join SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.BRONZE.stg_ctxepicorkinetic__company_enrollment as gate
    on source.company_code = gate.company_code
where source.company_code <> '000000'  -- junk placeholder company, not a real enrolled company

-- Bronze: Kinetic labor detail -- the Kinetic fact source.
-- Thin rename only, no business logic. Gated by the enrollment view (SD-10), not a
-- hardcoded company list. Carries Epicor's native EARNEDHRS through as a plain column --
-- NOT treated as authoritative earned hours (SD-11). The real derivation happens in
-- int_labor_standard_hours (Silver), from the operation's per-unit standard x quantity
-- produced. This column exists here only so Silver can cross-check against it later.
--
-- SD-22: job_num, employee_num, resource_group_key, operation_code are normalized with
-- upper(trim()) -- the same real-world key is stored with inconsistent casing across rows
-- in the raw source (confirmed empirically, e.g. 'BPQ45915' vs 'bpq45915'). Case-sensitive
-- joins on these columns silently drop matched rows. See PROJECT_LOG.md SD-22/SD-23.

with source as (

    select
        company                 as company_code,
        laborhedseq             as labor_header_seqnum,
        labordtlseq             as labor_detail_seqnum,
        upper(trim(employeenum)) as employee_num,
        labortype               as labor_type_code,
        labortypepseudo         as labor_type_pseudo,
        rework                  as is_rework,
        upper(trim(jobnum))     as job_num,
        assemblyseq             as assembly_seqnum,
        oprseq                  as operation_seqnum,
        upper(trim(opcode))     as operation_code,
        upper(trim(jcdept))      as jc_dept,
        upper(trim(resourcegrpid)) as resource_group_key,
        laborhrs                as actual_hours,
        burdenhrs               as burden_hours,
        laborqty                as quantity_produced,
        scrapqty                as quantity_scrapped,
        earnedhrs               as native_earned_hours_crosscheck,
        complete                as is_complete,
        opcomplete              as is_operation_complete,
        clockindate             as clock_in_date_text,
        payrolldate             as payroll_date_text,
        fiscalyear              as fiscal_year,
        fiscalperiod            as fiscal_period,
        postedtogl              as is_posted_to_gl,
        wipposted               as is_wip_posted,
        laborrate               as labor_rate,
        burdenrate              as burden_rate,
        sysrevid                as _sysrevid
    from MATILLION_RAW.CRETEX_EPICOR_KINETIC.ERP_LABORDTL

)

-- No is_incremental() filter: the source is a full flush-and-fill snapshot (SD-03), so
-- every run re-presents the full filtered set and the merge's unique_key does the
-- row-level insert/update. This does not handle source-side deletes -- acceptable for
-- now, revisit if that becomes material.

select source.*, current_timestamp() as _loaded_at
from source
inner join SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.BRONZE.stg_ctxepicorkinetic__company_enrollment as gate
    on source.company_code = gate.company_code

-- Silver/intermediate: per-unit Production rate and operation-level Setup credit for every
-- Kinetic job operation.
--
-- SD-26 (REVISED FOUNDATION -- replaces SD-14/SD-19/SD-23/SD-24): the prior several
-- iterations of this model (a 9-way STANDARD_FORMAT conversion from PRODSTANDARD; an
-- operation-level QUANTITY_COMPLETED-driven earned_hours; a conditional zero-standard
-- setup-credit rule) were all built by reverse-engineering empirically from reconciliation
-- data, not from the actual documented business rule. Reading production's own Silver
-- column comments directly (CTX_EARNED_HOURS_PRD.SILVER.FACT_LABOR) plus the Cretex
-- Medallion PoC Earned Hours Business Design Document surfaced the real rule, which is
-- simpler than anything previously built here:
--
--   Production-type labor (labortypepseudo='P', non-rework): earns
--   quantity_produced * (est_production_hours / run_quantity) per transaction.
--   Kinetic's standard rate is read directly from Epicor's own pre-computed
--   est_production_hours, NOT re-derived from PRODSTANDARD/STANDARD_FORMAT -- Epicor
--   already applied whatever internal format math applies when it computed that
--   estimate, so re-deriving it from raw fields was duplicating (and, per the 87.67%
--   agreement rate measured empirically, occasionally disagreeing with) work Epicor had
--   already done correctly.
--
--   Setup-type labor (labortypepseudo='S', non-rework): earns a FIXED amount per
--   OPERATION (never multiplied by quantity -- "Setup is a FIXED amount per operation,
--   so dividing it by pieces is a category error", per production's own column
--   documentation), credited ONCE regardless of how many Setup labor transactions exist
--   on that operation. This mirrors a documented historical defect in the Cretex
--   business-design process itself: multiple Setup time entries against the same
--   operation were once double/multiply-counting the setup budget (job 200013 op 21,
--   a 5-hour setup estimate, was being accumulated across 13 labor entries before this
--   was caught and fixed -- variance against Epicor's native EARNEDHRS improved from
--   +223% to +0.6% for affected operations). The earned amount is
--   est_setup_hours * (1.0 if the operation or job is complete, else
--   setup_pct_complete / 100.0) -- SETUPPCTCOMPLETE is Epicor's own cumulative
--   percent-complete field for the setup function on that operation.
--
--   EARNED_HOURS_RAW_UNPRORATED / PERCENT_ALLOCATED (production's proration columns) are
--   confirmed ProfitKey-specific (NULL on Kinetic, which has no equivalent) -- that
--   mechanism is correctly out of scope here.
--
-- Validated against production's actual EARNED_HOURS_JOB_OPERATION, full 3-company
-- population, before implementing: CDT 95.23% match (+0.20% aggregate), QTS 100.00%
-- match (~0.0% aggregate), CCR 96.89% match (+0.10% aggregate) -- an order of magnitude
-- better than every prior empirically-reverse-engineered iteration (best prior: CDT
-- 78.62%/+2.58%, QTS 99.71%/-0.67%, CCR 71.88%/-1.99%).
--
-- This model now carries the Production RATE (per-unit) and the Setup CREDIT
-- (operation-level, already a final amount, not a rate) side by side -- they combine
-- additively at the fct_labor grain, not here, since Production is transaction-driven
-- and Setup is operation-driven.

with job_operation as (

    select *
    from SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.BRONZE.stg_ctxepicorkinetic__job_operation

)

select
    company_code,
    job_num,
    assembly_seqnum,
    operation_seqnum,
    operation_code,
    run_quantity,
    quantity_completed,
    est_production_hours,
    est_production_hours / nullif(run_quantity, 0) as production_std_hours_per_unit,  -- SD-26

    est_setup_hours,
    setup_pct_complete,
    is_operation_complete,
    is_job_complete,
    est_setup_hours
        * case
            when is_operation_complete then 1.0  -- SD-26: OPERATION completion only, NOT job completion -- confirmed empirically (job 201143 op 10: jobcomplete=TRUE but opcomplete=FALSE, setuppctcomplete=0, and production credits 0, not the full est_setup_hours)
            else coalesce(setup_pct_complete, 0) / 100.0
          end as setup_earned_hours_credit,                                           -- SD-26

    is_subcontract
from job_operation

-- Silver/intermediate: recomputed labor fact at the labor-transaction grain.
--
-- SD-26 (REVISED FOUNDATION): earned_hours is now computed for BOTH Production and Setup
-- direct labor, per the corrected business rule (see int_labor_standard_hours header) --
-- NOT just Production as SD-13 assumed. Indirect/Move still earn 0 (a real zero, no
-- standard applies to them, matching production's own IS_DIRECT_LABOR definition).
-- Rework still earns 0 at this grain (SD-13's rework exclusion is unaffected by SD-26).
--
-- Production (labor_type_pseudo='P', non-rework): earned_hours = quantity_produced *
-- production_std_hours_per_unit, computed per transaction (transaction grain is correct
-- -- confirmed directly against production's own SILVER.FACT_LABOR, which is itself a
-- transaction-grain rollup, not an operation-level QUANTITY_COMPLETED-driven calculation
-- as SD-19/23 assumed).
--
-- Setup (labor_type_pseudo='S', non-rework): earned_hours is NOT computed per transaction
-- here -- it is a FIXED, OPERATION-level amount (setup_earned_hours_credit, from
-- int_labor_standard_hours) that must be credited exactly ONCE per operation regardless of
-- how many Setup labor transactions exist on it. Carrying the per-operation credit through
-- on every Setup row here (rather than summing it per-transaction) would double/multiply
-- count it when this table is later aggregated -- exactly the historical defect this rule
-- corrects for (see int_labor_standard_hours header, job 200013 op 21). fct_labor is
-- responsible for adding this credit in ONCE per operation (e.g. via MAX(), not SUM()),
-- not by summing this column across Setup rows.
--
-- earned_hours can be LEGITIMATELY NEGATIVE (reversal/correction labor transactions carry
-- negative quantity_produced -- confirmed against live data: all negative cases trace to
-- negative quantity_produced with a positive standard rate, never a negative rate) and
-- LEGITIMATELY NULL for Production rows whose operation standard is unresolved (no
-- matching ERP_JOBOPER row, or a zero run_quantity denominator -- flagged via
-- has_unresolved_standard below rather than silently defaulted to zero, per "flag bad
-- data, don't silently fix it").
--
-- native_earned_hours_crosscheck (Epicor's own EARNEDHRS, carried from Bronze) is kept
-- for comparison only -- never treated as the reported figure (SD-11).

with labor as (

    select *
    from SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.BRONZE.stg_ctxepicorkinetic__labor_detail

),

standard_hours as (

    select *
    from SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.SILVER.int_labor_standard_hours

),

job_header as (

    select company_code, job_num, is_mrp_planning_job
    from SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.BRONZE.stg_ctxepicorkinetic__job_header

)

select
    labor.company_code,
    labor.job_num,
    labor.assembly_seqnum,
    labor.operation_seqnum,
    labor.labor_header_seqnum,
    labor.labor_detail_seqnum,
    labor.employee_num,
    labor.jc_dept,
    labor.resource_group_key,
    labor.labor_type_code,
    labor.labor_type_pseudo,
    labor.is_rework,
    labor.quantity_produced,
    labor.quantity_scrapped,
    labor.actual_hours,
    labor.burden_hours,
    labor.clock_in_date_text,
    labor.payroll_date_text,
    labor.fiscal_year,
    labor.fiscal_period,
    job_header.is_mrp_planning_job,

    standard_hours.production_std_hours_per_unit,
    case
        when labor.labor_type_code = 'S' and not labor.is_rework
            then standard_hours.setup_earned_hours_credit
        else null
    end as setup_earned_hours_credit,                                                  -- SD-26: only exposed on Setup rows, so fct_labor's MAX() naturally scopes the credit to operations with a real Setup transaction -- not every operation that happens to have a populated est_setup_hours

    case
        when labor.labor_type_code = 'P' and not labor.is_rework
            then labor.quantity_produced * standard_hours.production_std_hours_per_unit
        else 0
    end as earned_hours,                                                             -- SD-26

    (labor.labor_type_code = 'P' and not labor.is_rework
        and standard_hours.production_std_hours_per_unit is null) as has_unresolved_standard,

    labor.native_earned_hours_crosscheck

from labor
left join standard_hours
    on  labor.company_code      = standard_hours.company_code
    and labor.job_num           = standard_hours.job_num
    and labor.assembly_seqnum   = standard_hours.assembly_seqnum
    and labor.operation_seqnum  = standard_hours.operation_seqnum
left join job_header
    on  labor.company_code = job_header.company_code
    and labor.job_num      = job_header.job_num

-- Gold: the central fact, aggregated to company + job + assembly_seqnum + operation_seqnum
-- -- the SAME grain as the reconciliation target (CTX_EARNED_HOURS_PRD.GOLD.
-- EARNED_HOURS_JOB_OPERATION), confirmed via its own column list, so the next
-- (reconciliation) step can compare row-for-row without a re-aggregation first.
--
-- department is deliberately NOT joined here -- production's own target grain doesn't
-- carry it either (dim_department exists for future grains, not this one).
--
-- earned_hours is now the sum of two components (SD-26, replaces SD-19/SD-23/SD-24):
-- (1) Production labor's per-transaction earned_hours, summed normally (transaction grain
--     is correct, confirmed against production's own SILVER.FACT_LABOR); and
-- (2) Setup's operation-level credit, added in ONCE via MAX() -- never SUM() -- since it is
--     a fixed per-operation amount, not a per-transaction one. Summing it would
--     double/multiply-count it across however many Setup labor transactions exist on the
--     operation, which is the exact historical defect this rule corrects for (see
--     int_labor_standard_hours header). See that model's header for the corrected
--     root-cause history and the empirical validation (CDT 95.23%, QTS 100.00%, CCR
--     96.89% match against production, all 3 companies).

with labor as (

    select *
    from SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.SILVER.int_labor_detail

),

standard_hours as (

    select company_code, job_num, assembly_seqnum, operation_seqnum, quantity_completed
    from SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.SILVER.int_labor_standard_hours

),

job_header as (

    select company_code, job_num, part_num, part_revision, is_mrp_planning_job
    from SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.BRONZE.stg_ctxepicorkinetic__job_header

),

part as (

    select company_id, part_key, part_revision, part_dim_key
    from SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.GOLD.dim_part

),

labor_with_part as (

    select
        labor.*,
        job_header.part_num,
        job_header.part_revision,
        part.part_dim_key
    from labor
    left join job_header
        on  labor.company_code = job_header.company_code
        and labor.job_num      = job_header.job_num
    left join part
        on  job_header.company_code                                     = part.company_id
        and job_header.part_num                                         = upper(trim(part.part_key))
        and coalesce(job_header.part_revision, '')                      = coalesce(upper(trim(part.part_revision)), '')

),

aggregated as (

    select
        company_code,
        job_num,
        assembly_seqnum,
        operation_seqnum,
        max(part_dim_key)                                               as part_dim_key,
        max(is_mrp_planning_job)                                        as is_mrp_planning_job,

        count(*)                                                        as labor_txns,
        count(distinct employee_num)                                    as employees_involved,

        sum(actual_hours)                                               as actual_hours,
        sum(quantity_produced)                                          as txn_summed_quantity_produced,
        sum(earned_hours)                                               as production_earned_hours,        -- SD-26
        max(setup_earned_hours_credit)                                  as setup_earned_hours,              -- SD-26: MAX, not SUM
        sum(case when has_unresolved_standard then 1 else 0 end)        as txns_no_computable_standard,

        min(try_cast(clock_in_date_text as date))                       as first_labor_date,
        max(try_cast(clock_in_date_text as date))                       as last_labor_date,

        sum(native_earned_hours_crosscheck)                             as native_earned_hours_crosscheck

    from labor_with_part
    group by company_code, job_num, assembly_seqnum, operation_seqnum

)

select
    aggregated.*,
    coalesce(aggregated.production_earned_hours, 0) + coalesce(aggregated.setup_earned_hours, 0) as earned_hours,  -- SD-26
    standard_hours.quantity_completed                                   as quantity_produced
from aggregated
left join standard_hours
    on  aggregated.company_code     = standard_hours.company_code
    and aggregated.job_num          = standard_hours.job_num
    and aggregated.assembly_seqnum  = standard_hours.assembly_seqnum
    and aggregated.operation_seqnum = standard_hours.operation_seqnum

-- Reconciliation (diagnostic, point-in-time -- NOT a permanent pipeline layer). Compares
-- this build's fct_labor against the production reconciliation target at the SAME grain:
-- company+job+operation_seqnum (LOT is always NULL for Kinetic -- confirmed against live
-- data, so it is dropped; assembly_seqnum is summed away here too -- checked that every
-- job+operation combo with >1 assembly is an MRP-D% placeholder planning job with zero
-- real labor, so this causes no practical divergence for real production jobs).
--
-- This view's purpose is transitional: once a decision is made on this build vs.
-- production, it has done its job and can be retired -- unlike Bronze/Silver/Gold, which
-- are meant to persist regardless of outcome.

with shadow as (

    select
        company_code,
        job_num,
        operation_seqnum,
        sum(earned_hours)                     as earned_hours,
        sum(actual_hours)                     as actual_hours,
        sum(quantity_produced)                as quantity_produced,
        sum(labor_txns)                        as labor_txns,
        max(employees_involved)                as employees_involved,
        sum(txns_no_computable_standard)       as txns_no_computable_standard,
        max(is_mrp_planning_job)               as is_mrp_planning_job,
        max(case when part_dim_key is null then 1 else 0 end) as part_unmatched
    from SANDBOX_EARNEDHOURS_SHADOW.GOLD.fct_labor
    group by company_code, job_num, operation_seqnum

),

production as (

    select
        company_code,
        job                                    as job_num,
        operation_seqnum,
        earned_hours                           as prod_earned_hours,
        actual_hours                           as prod_actual_hours,
        quantity_produced                      as prod_quantity_produced,
        labor_txns                             as prod_labor_txns,
        employees_involved                     as prod_employees_involved
    from CTX_EARNED_HOURS_PRD.GOLD.EARNED_HOURS_JOB_OPERATION
    where company_code in ('CTX11002', 'CTX11003', 'CTX11101')

)

select
    coalesce(shadow.company_code, production.company_code)      as company_code,
    coalesce(shadow.job_num, production.job_num)                as job_num,
    coalesce(shadow.operation_seqnum, production.operation_seqnum) as operation_seqnum,

    shadow.earned_hours                        as shadow_earned_hours,
    production.prod_earned_hours,
    shadow.earned_hours - production.prod_earned_hours            as delta,
    case
        when production.prod_earned_hours = 0 or production.prod_earned_hours is null then null
        else (shadow.earned_hours - production.prod_earned_hours) / abs(production.prod_earned_hours)
    end                                         as pct_diff,

    case
        when shadow.company_code is null then 'ONLY_IN_PROD'
        when production.company_code is null then 'ONLY_IN_SHADOW'
        when abs(coalesce(shadow.earned_hours, 0) - coalesce(production.prod_earned_hours, 0)) <= 0.01 then 'MATCH'
        else 'MISMATCH'
    end                                         as match_category,

    shadow.actual_hours                        as shadow_actual_hours,
    production.prod_actual_hours,
    shadow.quantity_produced                   as shadow_quantity_produced,
    production.prod_quantity_produced,
    shadow.labor_txns                          as shadow_labor_txns,
    production.prod_labor_txns,

    shadow.txns_no_computable_standard,
    shadow.part_unmatched,
    shadow.is_mrp_planning_job

from shadow
full outer join production
    on  shadow.company_code     = production.company_code
    and shadow.job_num          = production.job_num
    and shadow.operation_seqnum = production.operation_seqnum
